title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 93-95). X/S is a smooth relative curve and ω = Ω^1_{X/S}. On the previous page Grothendieck built an extension 0→Ω→𝓛→O_X→0, with Ω≅ω and 𝓛 ≅ P^1_{X/S}(ω)⊗ω^{-1}. He also built a first-order operator c_Ω, and a rank-3 bundle 𝒱 filtered with graded pieces Ω, Ω^0=O, Ω^{-1}; this is in effect Sym^2 of a rank-2 jet bundle, i.e. the adjoint bundle of an sl_2-oper. The 'admissible' connections on 𝒱 extending c_Ω form a torsor under Ω⊗ω ≅ ω^{⊗2}. This torsor is the classical torsor of projective connections. The canonical P^1-bundle is P = P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)), with a distinguished section σ (the oper flag).

This page, §1.5, 'Sections horizontales de P'. Questions: for which projective connections does P have horizontal sections, and what are they? He restricts to horizontal sections disjoint from σ.
- A section of P−σ(X) is the same as a splitting of 𝓛, i.e. of P^1_{X/S}(ω).
- Such a splitting refines the filtration to a direct-sum decomposition 𝒱 ≅ Ω⊕Ω^0⊕Ω^{-1}.
- Choose a local basis δ of Ω. An admissible connection c is then described by three forms ϖ_2, ϖ_1, ϖ_0 with values in Ω⊗ω, ω and Ω^{-1}⊗ω.
- The ϖ_2-component (in Ω⊗ω ≅ ω^2) is the obstruction to horizontality of the chosen section. It can be killed in exactly one way by changing c by an element ω_2 ∈ Γ(Ω⊗ω), using the torsor structure.

Prop. (2 assumed invertible, 'canonical' case). For each splitting of 𝓛 there is exactly one admissible (projective) connection for which the corresponding section of P is horizontal. This gives a map {sections of P−σ(X)} = {splittings of P^1_{X/S}(ω)} → {projective connections}. Its image is the set of projective connections admitting a horizontal section disjoint from σ.

Next page, in a coordinate t: s_0+λ dt ↦ c_0 + (dλ/dt + λ^2) dt^2, with a 'facteur 2 ?' query. So existence of such a horizontal section amounts to solving the Riccati equation λ' + λ^2 = φ. Poles of λ correspond to points where the section meets σ.

In modern terms this is the sl_2 Miura-oper correspondence. A Miura oper is an oper together with a horizontal reduction generic relative to the oper flag. The map to opers is the Miura transformation, here a Riccati map, formulated algebraically over an arbitrary base where 2 is invertible.
errors: The text's 'identification' is too strong if read as a bijection; Grothendieck himself struck out 'correspondance bijective'. The map from splittings to projective connections is not injective. A connection admitting one horizontal section disjoint from σ admits locally a one-parameter family (Riccati solutions with arbitrary initial value). Only the 'image' statement is correct.

The normalisation is unsettled: Grothendieck flags 'facteur 2 ?' in the next-page formula λ'+λ^2. This depends on the identification Ω≅ω (via -2, needing 2 invertible); constants are not fixed on the page.
The page assumes 2 invertible (margin '2 inv. !'). The previous page asks whether this is really necessary, and that remains unresolved.

ideas.what: Projective connections on a relative curve as a torsor under ω^{⊗2}, realised as admissible connections on a filtered rank-3 bundle built from P^1_{X/S}(ω)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1960s, projective structures); Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s); Mochizuki (indigenous bundles in arithmetic setting)

ideas.what: Sections of the P^1-bundle P disjoint from the oper section σ ↔ splittings of the jet bundle P^1_{X/S}(ω); unique connection making a given such section horizontal; projective connections admitting such a section = image
ideas.modern_name: Miura opers (oper + generic horizontal Borel reduction) and the Miura map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Miura (1968, KdV); Drinfeld–Sokolov (1985); E. Frenkel (Miura opers, ~2003)

ideas.what: Local formula reducing existence of such horizontal sections to the Riccati equation λ'+λ^2=φ; poles of λ = intersection points with σ

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, ca. 1972 and algebraically over a general base S with 2 invertible, what is now called the Miura-oper correspondence for sl_2. These are horizontal sections of the oper P^1-bundle generic with respect to the oper flag. He shows the corresponding connection is uniquely determined by a splitting of P^1_{X/S}(ω), and that the map is given locally by the Riccati operator. This predates Drinfeld–Sokolov and Frenkel's 'Miura opers'.
missed.quote: il y a une et une seule conn. admissible sur 𝒱 (ou P...) pour laquelle la section correspondante de P sont horizontales
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority rather than new mathematics: the construction is now standard. Placed in a file on Gauss–Manin and the Cartier operator, it also suggests the char-p version (Miura opers versus p-curvature and dormant opers, Mochizuki/Wakabayashi). That arithmetic link was developed much later and without credit to this source.

missed.claim: Whether the hypothesis '2 invertible' is necessary is raised (previous-page margin, 'cela est-il vraiment nécessaire') and not settled.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Opers and projective structures in characteristic 2 are delicate, and only partially treated in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, unpublished algebraic formulation of sl_2 Miura opers and the Riccati/Miura map over a general base, dating from about 1972 and in a Cartier-operator context. The mathematics is now standard (Gunning, Drinfeld–Sokolov, Frenkel, Mochizuki), so the interest is historical priority and context, not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'connexions ∇ injectables' should almost certainly read 'connexions projectives sur X/S'.
'∇ ≃ Ω⊕Ω^0⊕Ω^{-1}' and '𝒟' denote the rank-3 bundle 𝒱 (written V), not a connection ∇.
'Θ' throughout is the tensor product ⊗ (e.g. Ω⊗ω, Ω^{-1}⊗ω).
'Celle correspondant donc à une décomposition de 𝒟' should read roughly 'Elles correspondent donc à une décomposition de 𝒱 en somme directe'.
